definition: 2020 Census incorporated place/city; Washington uses the District of Columbia place.
block: populated 2020 city-limit Census blocks; tract: populated city-limit tract portions. NYC also uses tracts here, unlike its 70-section PSSI model.
Maximum great-circle distance between connected representative points, in kilometers. No self-links.
Number of populated geographic units in the distance-based Fryer model; differs from PSSI for block models and NYC.
2020 Census category. White, Black and Asian alone include Hispanic residents; Hispanic is any race. Categories overlap.
Nᵣ / N, where N is the total city population across all tract portions. Fraction from 0 to 1; used in every adjustment.

Distance-based geographic-neighbor SSI, radius 1 km, dominant category assignment, equal all-neighbor weights, no self-links. Component eigenvalues averaged by eligible assigned-node count; geographic isolates excluded.
Distance Fryer SSI minus all-city category population fraction K. Requested adjustment, not simulated null baseline.
(Distance Fryer SSI - K) / (1 - K). K is all-city category population fraction; negative values retained.
Nodes assigned to this category that have at least one neighbor of any category. This is the unweighted city SSI averaging denominator.
ok or undefined_no_eligible_assigned_nodes. Undefined scores are blank/NaN, not zero.
Largest absolute component eigenpair residual across this category in this geographic graph.
New distance-based Fryer SSI minus the previous 1 km score. Transit does not change the graph, so this should be numerical zero.
